status: editorial research; not published lesson copy
purpose: A source-backed teaching plan for the 20-lesson UX course. Notes are original paraphrases and links, not scraped article text.

currentCourseAudit.mainProblem: The primary example changes almost every lesson. Concepts such as mental models, triangulation, service blueprints, and hypotheses arrive with little beginner explanation or continuity.

runningCase.name: Clinic appointment and check-in service
runningCase.scope: A person books an appointment, prepares, arrives, checks in, waits, receives updates, and gets help when the service fails. Staff and system handoffs are part of the same case.
runningCase.evidenceRule: Case facts supplied for an exercise are fictional. Never present them as findings from a real study. Give learners a small evidence packet before asking them to infer a cause or choose a design.

editorialRules: Begin with the learner's immediate question and a concrete scene before naming a method.
Define each new term in ordinary language and show its use in the running case.
Move from observation to interpretation to decision; mark uncertainty at each step.
Keep one cumulative artifact: the clinic task map becomes a research plan, problem frame, design, test plan, revision, and final decision record.
Use original teaching text with visible attribution and a short reading list. Link to source articles; do not reproduce their prose, figures, or examples wholesale.
Use a second context only after the clinic example is understood, as a transfer exercise.
Have a human subject reviewer check factual claims, beginner comprehension, source fit, and whether the exercise can be answered from the material taught.

ux_definition.title: The Definition of User Experience (UX)
ux_definition.note: Use to distinguish a person's whole experience from interface usability.

ux_basics.title: UX Basics: Study Guide
ux_basics.note: Beginner reading sequence and vocabulary check.

mental_models.title: Mental Models
mental_models.note: What a person believes the system will do and how mismatch affects behavior.

heuristics.title: 10 Usability Heuristics for User Interface Design
heuristics.note: System status, error prevention, and recovery as checks rather than recipes.

access_intro.title: Introduction to Web Accessibility
access_intro.note: Define access by whether people can perceive, understand, navigate, and act.

access_stories.title: Stories of Web Users
access_stories.note: Concrete variation in people, tools, and barriers; pair these illustrations with testing.

trust_form.title: Establish trust
trust_form.note: Explain why sensitive information is requested, what is needed, and what happens to it.

field_observation.title: Contextual research and observation
field_observation.note: Observe a real task in context and record what is seen separately from what is inferred.

research_questions.title: Capturing research questions
research_questions.note: Start method selection with an uncertainty the team can act on.

triangulation.title: Triangulation: Get Better Research Results by Using Multiple UX Methods
triangulation.note: Use different evidence types to test an explanation's limits.

analysis.title: Analyse a research session
analysis.note: Move from notes to observations, findings, and actions in clear steps.

problem_statement.title: Problem Statements in UX Discovery
problem_statement.note: Frame affected people, the problem, and consequence while leaving unproven causes open.

discovery.title: User research in discovery
discovery.note: Explore current behavior and the full service before proposing a solution.

service_intro.title: Designing good government services: an introduction
service_intro.note: Consider a service from beginning to end, front to back, and across channels.

journey_flow.title: User Journeys vs. User Flows
journey_flow.note: Connect the broad journey with the detailed sequence for one task.

imitating.title: The Risks of Imitating Designs
imitating.note: Treat familiar patterns as candidates and test their fit in the current setting.

parallel_design.title: 3 Design Processes for High Usability: Iterative Design, Parallel Design, and Competitive Testing
parallel_design.note: Compare multiple plausible designs before committing to one.

interface_writing.title: Writing for user interfaces
interface_writing.note: Put the important action and state in plain, concise language.

error_messages.title: Error-Message Guidelines
error_messages.note: Make failure visible, understandable, and recoverable.

prototype.title: Paper Prototyping: Getting User Data Before You Code
prototype.note: Choose the simplest representation that still permits the intended observation.

prototype_fidelity.title: UX Prototypes: Low Fidelity vs. High Fidelity
prototype_fidelity.note: Match prototype realism to what must be learned.

test_planning.title: Using moderated usability testing
test_planning.note: Write believable, neutral tasks that answer a research question.

test_tasks.title: Writing Tasks for Quantitative and Qualitative Usability Studies
test_tasks.note: Task wording depends on whether the goal is exploratory or measurement.

findings.title: Making Usability Findings Actionable
findings.note: Report an observed issue with context and a direction the team can use.

iteration.title: Iterative Design of User Interfaces
iteration.note: Revise, observe again, and keep unresolved questions visible.

sharing.title: Sharing user research findings
sharing.note: Bring evidence into team decisions while it can still affect the work.

constraints.title: How the discovery phase works
constraints.note: Surface policy, technical, and organizational constraints before choosing scope.

joined_channels.title: Provide a joined up experience across all channels
joined_channels.note: Coordinate digital, phone, paper, and face-to-face help as needed by users.

blueprint.title: Service Blueprints: Definition
blueprint.note: Make visible the staff, systems, and processes behind a touchpoint.

lessons.entryQuestion: What is the person trying to finish, beyond using the kiosk?
lessons.teach: Introduce UX through one patient's journey from appointment reminder to being called; separate the kiosk interaction from the service outcome.
lessons.caseBeat: Draw the first task map with the patient, staff, and appointment system as distinct actors.
lessons.artifact: Task map v1 with the moment the patient can know check-in succeeded.

lessons.entryQuestion: How does the patient know what the kiosk will do and whether it worked?
lessons.teach: Define expectation, action, system state, feedback, and recovery in that order; use the same check-in submission to show each.
lessons.caseBeat: Compare 'Done' with a receipt-backed status and a delayed state.
lessons.artifact: Annotated check-in state sequence.

lessons.entryQuestion: Who cannot complete check-in under the current conditions?
lessons.teach: Start with the task and setting, then examine barriers to perceiving, operating, understanding, and recovering; avoid treating one alternative as universal.
lessons.caseBeat: Assess a noisy entrance, glare, short timeout, language, and a patient who needs help without exposing health details.
lessons.artifact: Barrier and alternative map for the same check-in flow.

lessons.entryQuestion: What does the patient need to know before providing sensitive information?
lessons.teach: Connect trust to clear purpose, data use, progress, truthful status, and a safe help route; calibrate review to consequence.
lessons.caseBeat: Review a kiosk request for date of birth and a medication question; distinguish identity verification from unnecessary collection.
lessons.artifact: Trust and consequence review of the current flow.

lessons.entryQuestion: What actually happens when people arrive?
lessons.teach: Define observation versus interpretation; prepare a short contextual observation plan before judging interface quality.
lessons.caseBeat: Observe check-in in a crowded reception area, including staff workarounds and people who bypass the kiosk.
lessons.artifact: Observation log with separate facts, quotes, and open questions.

lessons.entryQuestion: Which evidence would reduce the most important uncertainty?
lessons.teach: Pair specific questions with observation, interviews, service data, or usability tasks; explain what each source cannot establish.
lessons.caseBeat: Investigate whether failed check-ins come from unclear confirmation, data mismatch, or the staff handoff.
lessons.artifact: Question-to-evidence matrix with limitations.

lessons.entryQuestion: Does the observed hesitation have one cause?
lessons.teach: Sort observations, interpretations, and competing explanations; seek a piece of evidence that would tell explanations apart.
lessons.caseBeat: A patient waits beside the kiosk after seeing a success message; consider uncertainty, instructions, and a missed staff update.
lessons.artifact: Three hypotheses and a discriminating research question for each.

lessons.entryQuestion: What problem can the team responsibly claim to be solving?
lessons.teach: Write affected person, task, observed difficulty, consequence, and what remains unproven before naming a solution.
lessons.caseBeat: Use the accumulated evidence packet to frame the check-in and waiting problem.
lessons.artifact: Evidence-backed problem statement with explicit uncertainty.

lessons.entryQuestion: Where does the proposed change sit in the whole appointment journey?
lessons.teach: Show a journey map before a detailed flow; trace entry, check-in, acknowledgment, waiting, and help across channels.
lessons.caseBeat: Add the staff system and reception desk to the patient's route.
lessons.artifact: Journey map and one detailed check-in flow.

lessons.entryQuestion: What are three credible ways to confirm check-in?
lessons.teach: Generate alternatives from the stated problem, then compare them against user context, failure modes, and constraints rather than popularity.
lessons.caseBeat: Compare kiosk confirmation, paper ticket, and staffed confirmation under realistic clinic conditions.
lessons.artifact: Option table with rationale and unresolved questions.

lessons.entryQuestion: What does the patient see if acknowledgment is delayed or fails?
lessons.teach: Specify initial, in-progress, confirmed, delayed, failed, and recovery states as one coherent interaction; write labels that match actual system state.
lessons.caseBeat: Design a queue delay and an unavailable staff system without falsely claiming success.
lessons.artifact: State inventory and annotated recovery flow.

lessons.entryQuestion: What must the prototype do to test this decision?
lessons.teach: Start with the research question and choose only the content and behavior needed to observe it; include consequential failure states.
lessons.caseBeat: Build a paper or clickable version of the proposed confirmation and delayed path.
lessons.artifact: Prototype plan listing what is simulated and what cannot be learned from it.

lessons.entryQuestion: What should change for patients if the redesign works?
lessons.teach: State the intended effect, the observable behavior, and a possible counterexample before testing; do not call a preference a result.
lessons.caseBeat: Predict that receipt-backed confirmation reduces repeated check-in and unnecessary reception queries.
lessons.artifact: Hypothesis and observation criteria tied to the design decision.

lessons.entryQuestion: How can a task reveal whether people understand check-in status?
lessons.teach: Write a believable scenario with a goal but no interface clues; recruit appropriate users and plan for accessibility and contextual limits.
lessons.caseBeat: Ask a participant arriving for an appointment to check in and decide what to do while confirmation is delayed.
lessons.artifact: Short moderated test plan and neutral task script.

lessons.entryQuestion: What do observed actions support, and what remains a guess?
lessons.teach: Keep observation, interpretation, impact, and confidence separate; report failures in context rather than turning a small study into a population claim.
lessons.caseBeat: Analyse a fictional packet of patient actions, comments, and staff observations from the prototype test.
lessons.artifact: Finding cards with evidence and a next question.

lessons.entryQuestion: Which change addresses the finding, and how will we check it?
lessons.teach: Trace a revision to a finding, name the intended mechanism, and set a follow-up task that could reveal remaining failure.
lessons.caseBeat: Revise an ambiguous delayed message and retest what patients infer about their place in the queue.
lessons.artifact: Before-and-after design decision with retest plan.

lessons.entryQuestion: What can the clinic team improve if the legacy system cannot acknowledge instantly?
lessons.teach: Separate a hard constraint from an assumption; stage improvements with owners and honest limitations.
lessons.caseBeat: Plan an interim provisional status, reception escalation, and longer-term system integration.
lessons.artifact: Staged decision with owner, dependency, and risk for each step.

lessons.entryQuestion: Will the advice still be true if a patient calls or asks staff?
lessons.teach: Use a service blueprint to connect patient-visible steps to frontstage staff, backstage systems, and recovery routes.
lessons.caseBeat: Align kiosk, SMS, reception, and call center language when appointments are delayed.
lessons.artifact: Small service blueprint with one failure path.

lessons.entryQuestion: Can someone outside the design team see why this approach was chosen?
lessons.teach: Present the problem, observed evidence, alternatives, chosen action, uncertainty, and next check in a short decision record.
lessons.caseBeat: Explain why the clinic chose receipt-backed confirmation and an interim route for outages.
lessons.artifact: One-page decision record linked to the research and test evidence.

lessons.entryQuestion: Can the learner improve the whole service with evidence and stated limits?
lessons.teach: Revisit the same case from person and goal through diagnosis, options, states, testing, and operational ownership; assess the chain of reasoning.
lessons.caseBeat: Use a new fictional evidence packet about a missed appointment caused by conflicting status across kiosk and reception.
lessons.artifact: Final service improvement proposal with map, problem frame, design, test, and decision record.
